_comment: Canonical survey definitions. The browser bundle imports this file and the
PocketBase route requires it, so a question exists in exactly one place:
copy, options, conditional logic, and validation limits all live here.
Adding a survey is adding a key under `forms` — no migration, no schema
change. Every response is stored as JSON under its form id and version, so
answers to a question that later changes stay readable under the version
that asked it. Bump that form's `version` whenever a question's meaning
changes; add a question freely without bumping, since absent keys read as
unanswered.
`questionSets` holds question lists more than one survey asks. A form takes
a set by name and may append its own `questions` after it, so the shared
questions stay word-for-word identical and answers stay comparable across
audiences. Editing a set edits every survey that uses it.
`audience`: 'public' accepts anonymous submissions; 'member' requires an
authenticated member and records who answered — say so in `privacyNote`,
because an attributed survey must not read as an anonymous one.
`appliesWhen`: the question is asked, and required, only while the named
question's answer satisfies `in` / `notIn`. Otherwise it is skipped and
stored as absent rather than empty. A question may only depend on one asked
before it.

core-discovery.prompt: Last time you were looking for somewhere to eat or drink, what did you actually do?
core-discovery.note: Choose the one closest to what happened.
core-discovery.error: Choose the one closest to what you actually did.

core-discovery.prompt: When did you last recommend a place to someone?
core-discovery.error: Choose when you last recommended a place.

core-discovery.prompt: If yes to that — how did you send it?
core-discovery.note: Skips itself if you can’t remember recommending one.

core-discovery.prompt: What’s annoying about how you find places now?
core-discovery.note: A sentence or two is plenty.
core-discovery.error: Tell us what gets in the way — even “nothing, honestly” helps.
core-discovery.placeholder: Be honest — too many tabs, reviews you can’t trust, lists you never open again. If nothing is broken, that is worth saying too.

discovery-habits.pageDescription: Four quick questions about how you find somewhere to eat or drink. Anyone can answer, anonymously — no account, and no need to know what Detour is.
discovery-habits.title: Good taste should travel.
discovery-habits.intro: Four quick questions about the last time you went looking for somewhere to eat or drink — and what gets in the way. You don’t need an account, and you don’t need to have heard of Detour.
discovery-habits.privacyNote: Anonymous by design. No account, no name, no email, no follow-up.
discovery-habits.submitNote: Every answer is required — question 3 only if it applies.

success.title: Thank you — that genuinely helps.
success.body: Nothing else happens now: there’s no account to confirm and no email to expect. Your answers go straight to the people building Detour.

friends.pageTitle: A few questions for friends — Detour
friends.pageDescription: A few blunt questions for the handful of people already in Detour, about whether it actually works.
friends.title: Be blunt with me.
friends.intro: Hey — you’re one of about five people in Detour right now, which makes you the only person who can tell me whether it actually works. A few things, and be properly blunt. I’d rather find out what’s wrong now than after I’ve built more of it.
friends.privacyNote: You’re signed in, so I’ll know it’s you.
friends.submitNote: Reply honestly — that’s the whole ask.

success.title: Thank you — that’s exactly what I needed.
success.body: If something was confusing, that’s the part I’ll go fix. — Olga

friends.signedOutNote: Sign in first — it’s the same login you used to join.

questions.prompt: First: what do you think Detour actually is? Explain it back to me in your own words.
questions.note: If it’s wrong, that’s my fault, not yours.
questions.error: A sentence is fine — just say it in your own words.
questions.placeholder: Whatever comes to mind first — don’t look it up.

questions.prompt: Is it interesting to you? Not “nice idea, well done” — would you actually open it.
questions.note: If the answer is no or a shrug, say that. It’s the most useful thing you could tell me.
questions.error: Yes, no, or a shrug — whichever is true.

questions.prompt: Honestly — is it just easier to Google it? Or ask someone in a group chat?
questions.note: If Detour is more effort than what you already do, I want to know — that’s the thing that kills it.
questions.error: Pick whichever is closest to true.

options.label: Yes — I’d just search or Google it
Yes — I’d ask a group chat
Not sure yet, Detour might be actually easier

questions.prompt: How often could you imagine actually using it?
Have you added a place yet?
questions.error: Yes or not yet — either is fine.

questions.note: Any of these is a fine answer. I’m not fishing for guilt.

options.label: Didn’t think anyone would see it

questions.prompt: And anything that felt confusing or pointless?
questions.note: Really, say it. Leave it blank if nothing comes to mind.
questions.placeholder: Anything that made you hesitate, or that seemed like busywork.

questions.prompt: Where do you keep going back to?
questions.note: The place you’ve taken more than one person. Name it, and what makes it worth the trip.
questions.error: Name one place — that’s the whole ask.
questions.placeholder: The place, and what makes it worth the trip.

founding-members.pageTitle: A few questions for founding members — Detour
founding-members.pageDescription: A few honest questions for the first fifty people in Detour, about whether it actually works.
founding-members.title: More promise than product.
founding-members.intro: You’re one of the first fifty people in Detour — thank you for taking a seat this early, when there’s more promise than product. What you think of it now matters more than what anyone thinks of it later.
founding-members.privacyNote: Not anonymous — you’re signed in, so this is recorded against your membership.
founding-members.submitNote: A few questions if you have five minutes. Honest answers are more useful to me than kind ones.
